title: Operator Reskilling & Synthetic Degradation Handoff Playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the program and operational contract for handing off synthetic-degradation experiments from the Platform Reliability Lab to oncall operators, and the reskilling pathway to certify operators to run, triage, and remediate those experiments in production-like environments. It pairs a reproducible validation pipeline, dashboard/alert contracts, and a structured learning path so operators gain decision autonomy without increasing mean time to recovery (MTTR).

Goals

- Reduce handoff friction between SRE experimenters and platform operators.
- Certify 90% of platform operators to independently run and respond to synthetic degradation scenarios within 3 months of program start.
- Keep MTTR for synthetic-degradation incidents <= 25 minutes during training windows.
- Maintain zero-customer-impact SLA for dark-tier experiments.

Scope

- Applies to experiments that intentionally exercise: cache warmset eviction, KV-prefix corruption injection, batch-eviction stress, model-variant fallback misfires, and regional prefetch failure modes.
- Excludes destructive data-migrations, PCI-scoped tests, and experiments targeting on-prem customer private deployments. Those remain in the Experimentation Review Board (ERB) path.

Ownership & Roles

- Platform Lab (owner): designs experiments, provides test harnesses, and signs off on synthetic scenarios.
- Oncall Operators (assignee): run scheduled experiments in staging/vestigated environments, practice triage, and perform documented mitigations.
- Platform Training (owner): runs the reskilling curriculum and certifies operators.
- Incident Commander (rotating): for experiments that cross a safety threshold and require escalation.

Prerequisites

1) Environment classification: run all experiments in environments tagged dark-, staging-, or canary-ops; never in prod unless ERB-approved and with a cross-org wartime plan.

2) Access: operators must have read access to the Platform Lab bucket, runbook repo, and operator-lab cluster namespace. Write access is granted only to certified operators (see Certification section).

3) Observability baseline: dashboards and traces listed in the Dashboard Contract must be green before launch.

Dashboard & Alert Contract

- Required dashboards (operator-facing):
  - Synthetic-Degradation Overview: 1m/5m token latency heatmap, KV cache hit ratio, batch queue depth, model swap rate.
  - Cost & Safety Overview: synthetic token volume vs. baseline, burst credits consumed, tenant-affinity score.
  - Escalation Signal Panel: experiment-safeguard metrics and derived signals.

- Mandatory alerts (examples):
  - alert:synthetic_degradation_latency_spike
    expr: increase(percentile_over_time(latency_1m, 5m), 300) > 20
    for: 2m
    severity: warning
    owner: platform-operator

  - alert:kv_cache_correctness_drop
    expr: kv_cache_correct_reads / kv_cache_total_reads < 0.98
    for: 1m
    severity: critical
    owner: platform-sre

- Safety thresholds (must be configured on experiment manifest):
  - tenant-error-rate <= 0.05% absolute above baseline
  - foreground-99th-latency <= 2x baseline (auto-abort if exceeded for > 60s)
  - synthetic-token-rate <= 5% of regional token ingress

Experiment Lifecycle (step-by-step)

1) Design & Review (Platform Lab)
  - Create experiment manifest (YAML) and attach risk analysis.
  - Run offline simulation in the lab harness until deterministic.
  - Present to ERB if risk > medium.

2) Operator Sandbox Run (Training)
  - Schedule 2-hour sandbox slot with an operator trainee and a Lab member.
  - Operator follows the Operator Checklist (below) under Lab supervision.
  - Lab annotates decisions and common failure modes for the training artifact.

3) Certified Operator Dry Run (Staging)
  - Certified operator executes a dry run in staging.
  - Platform Lab observes via the telemetry bridge and records artifacts.

4) Oncall Handoff (Canary-Ops/Dark)
  - Attach runbook link, dashboard snapshot, and experiment manifest to the run.
  - Notify oncall channel with pre-run digest (15 min prior).
  - Operator executes with an assigned Incident Commander on standby.

5) Post-Run Retrospective
  - Lab + operator complete a 2-question retrospective: what went well / risks observed.
  - If any safety threshold triggered, full incident postmortem is required.

Operator Checklist (to be completed during run)

- Pre-run
  - Verify dashboard green: latency, cache hit rate, queue depth.
  - Confirm safety thresholds configured in manifest.
  - Export dashboard snapshot and link to run ticket.

- During run
  - Monitor Escalation Signal Panel every 30s.
  - If warning-level alert fires, pause experiment and evaluate rollback gates.
  - If critical-level alert fires, abort experiment and trigger operator escalation.

- Post-run
  - Reconcile metrics to baseline.
  - Tag run artifacts with "operator-verified" and upload notes to the run ticket.
  - If regression detected, file a regression ticket and notify Platform Lab.

Certification & Training Pathway

- Level 1 (Observer): attend 2 sandbox sessions and pass a written checklist (read-only access).
- Level 2 (Runner): complete 3 supervised staging dry runs, pass a practical exam (execute & recover), granted temporary write tokens for lab namespace.
- Level 3 (Certified Operator): run 5 solo canary ops handoffs with no safety-threshold incidents and pass a scenario-based oral exam. Full write access and authority to sign off dark runs.

Training curriculum (8 weeks recommended cadence):
- Week 1: Observability primer for LLM workloads (dashboards, traces, token-cost panels).
- Week 2: Experiment manifests, safety gates, and manifests-in-practice labs.
- Week 3–4: Sandbox hands-on sessions (prefetch, KV eviction, model-swap stress).
- Week 5: Dry runs & practical exam.
- Week 6–7: Shadowing on-call during low-risk windows.
- Week 8: Final certification scenario and retrospective.

Runbook snippets & CLI examples

- Abort command (operator CLI):
  rwood operator run abort --run-id $RUN_ID --reason "safety-threshold-exceeded"

- Rollback to known-good model variant (example):
  rwood runtime model swap --service runtime-llm-v2 --from variant-experimental --to variant-stable --max-concurrency 50

- Snapshot dashboards to ticket (script):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://dashboards.internal/api/snapshots?panel=synthetic_overview&until=now > /tmp/run-${RUN_ID}-snap.json

Safety Escalation Matrix

- Warning alerts: platform-operator channel, operator on rotation triages within 5 minutes.
- Critical alerts: immediately page oncall SRE, Incident Commander engaged within 2 minutes.
- Cross-region customer bleed: executive pager and customer-success CSM briefed within 15 minutes.

Metrics & KPIs for Program Success

- Certification rate: percentage of operators reaching Level 3 within 3 months. Target: 75%.
- Training MTTR: median time-to-abort/rollback during training runs. Target: <= 25m.
- Experiment safety-trips: number of runs aborted due to safety thresholds per 100 runs. Target: < 5.
- Operational regression rate: number of post-run customer-impacting regressions per quarter. Target: 0.

Postmortem Triggers

- Any run that triggers a critical alert that impacts tenant-visible metrics (error-rate, 99th latency) requires a postmortem recorded in the Incident Reviews space within 48 hours.

Retrospective Cadence & Template

- Monthly: mini-retrospectives for Lab + operators to exchange learnings and update manifests.
- Quarterly: certification progress review and training syllabus refresh.

Retro template (required fields):
1) Run ID / Date
2) Scenario summary
3) What went well
4) What surprised us
5) Action items (owner + due date)
6) Safety threshold tuning suggestions

Examples & Case Studies (short)

1) KV eviction demo (2025-11-09): A canary run revealed an unexpected tenant-affinity regression when heatset coalescing threshold was lowered. Operator halted the experiment at t+4m; rollback avoided customer impact. Action: increase default safety threshold and add a pre-run tenant-affinity simulation step.

2) Model-variant misroute (2026-03-17): Synthetic model-swap caused a 1.8x spike in 99th latency for a regional cohort. Lab and operator updated the model-variant fallback DSL and created a stricter canary ramp schedule.

Governance & Change Control

- All experiment manifests must be stored in the experiments repo and tagged with an owner and risk level.
- High-risk experiments (risk > medium) require ERB approval and an oncall SRE as Incident Commander.
- Changes to the Dashboard & Alert Contract must be approved by Platform Observability maintainers and communicated 2 weeks prior to enforcement.

Appendix: Experiment Manifest Template (YAML snippet)

- name: kv-eviction-cohort-stress
  owner: platform-lab@redwood.com
  risk: low
  env: canary-ops
  safety_thresholds:
    tenant_error_rate_delta_pct: 0.05
    fg_99_latency_multiplier: 2.0
    synthetic_token_rate_pct: 5
  prechecks:
    - dashboard-green: synthetic_overview
    - kv_consistency: pass
  rollback_policy: immediate-abort
  notify: ['#platform-oncall', 'platform-lab']

Contact & Next Steps

- Questions or certification requests: platform-training@redwood.com
- To propose a new synthetic scenario: open an experiment PR in the experiments repo and add the label "proposed-experiment".

Document history

- 2026-01-12: Drafted by Priya Raman.
- 2026-03-18: Pilot run notes added (model-variant misroute).
- 2026-07-03: Published version with certification pathway and dashboard contract.
